items.body: Sudan Dudan is a Norwegian duo, Marit Karlberg and Anders Erik R�ine, who have released four albums over the last twenty years. On M�rke refrenger , their fifth, they are joined by Hans Hulb�kmo and Magnus Skavhaug Nergaard, contributing instrumentally and with the production. There are eight songs on the album with accompaniment principally led by acoustic guitar, augmented by fiddles, langeleik, lyre, jaws harp and more. The opening track, �Gard og grind� (�Fence and gate�) is a fine introduction to what is to come: finger-picked acoustic guitar, fiddle, bass and snare-drum played with brushes leading into the harmonized vocal, together creating an alluring sound drawing the listener in. M�rke refrenger by Sudan Dudan The mood of the album, reflected in its title which translates as �Dark Refrains,� is not always dark, but most of the material, including the title track, certainly has a reflective quality. According to the press release �the lyrics smoulder with unease about the present and the future, while looking back to the myths and riddles of the past. They speak of the earth, the sun, the moon, stars and planets, of lost brothers, quarrelling sisters, loss and grief, of the power of imagination, and of the answers to the simplest and most difficult riddles.� The lyrics of all the songs, in Norwegian, are included in the sleeve notes and while a hasty online translation can aid with some understanding, the full meanings tend to remain cryptic, but there is a sense that words and music complement each other. M�rke refrenger by Sudan Dudan For all its dark moodiness, M�rke refrenger does have its lighter moments. �Bagatelle� recalls and reinvents the melody of a well-known French song, adding some off-kilter harmonies, while �Rulleball� is more characteristically Norwegian, employing a vocal style known as tralling in which words are replaced by a vocalization of the melody, originally used to accompany dances when no instrument was available. No translation necessary there. M�rke refrenger by Sudan Dudan The final track �Skriften p� veggen� (�the writing on the wall�) features, for the only time on the album, electric guitar. The sound is deep and twangy, shades of Duane Eddy or a David Lynch soundtrack and it works very well. All in all a fine, imaginatively conceived and beautifully produced record, available as a download or vinyl. Find the artists online. items.body:
According to its founder, Eugene Rodriguez, who also sings and plays on the record, Los Cenzontles is a �musical group and non-profit organization, which I founded over thirty years ago.�  As he continues in the album�s liner notes, the group �has a long history of producing projects exploring Mexico�s deep roots and our connections with various traditions that, so far, have included Irish, Louisiana Creole, Cuban, American cowboy, classical, pop, rock, and blues�, the latest of which is
Adios Ke Aloha: Waves of the Same Sea
. Los Cenzontles translates to the mockingbird, or, from its Aztec root word, the bird of four hundred voices. This is a fitting name for the range of musical diversity represented here.
With songs sung in Spanish, Hawaiian, and English, the concept traces back to the legacy of Mexican cowboys who travelled from California to the Hawaiian Islands to wrangle the long-horned cattle introduced there in the nineteenth century. They also brought the guitar. The 16 tracks feature old Hawaiian songs with new Spanish lyrics, old Mexican songs with new Hawaiian lyrics, new compositions, and traditional Americana. Yet it is an entirely cohesive musical package held together by dense arrangements of ukuleles, guitars, Mexican harp, and accordion.
Sonny Lim & David Hidalgo
Besides their distinctive voices, the headline artists Taj Mahal and David Hidalgo provide the gravitas and musicianship that their long and distinguished careers have earned. According to the liner notes, they were the catalysts behind the project and facilitated the choice of songs, arrangements, and played a range of instruments. On vocals they are joined by Hawaiian natives Gary Haleamau, Sheldeen Haleamau, Sonny Lim, and long-time Cenzontles member Fabiola Trujillo.
Deportee
To give a taste of the sessions, included before the traditional �Fishin� Blues� is Taj Mahal teaching the musicians how to play it. Sung by David Hildalgo,  the lovely �A Matter of Time� comes from the 1984 album
Will the Wolf Survive
by his most famous project, Los Lobos. Another standout for me, �Navegar� features a slack string guitar solo reminiscent of Duane Eddie and one of many tasty lap steel turns by Sonny Lim. Their interpretation of Woody Guthrie's �Deportee� moves into social commentary, highlighting the cruel realities of being a migrant worker in America.
Vaquero Paniolo
Recorded over five days, mostly live in one room at the Los Cenzontles headquarters in San Pablo, California, including the talents of some of their academy�s students, the recording has real spontaneity to it. Arrangements are stretched by improvisations, sometimes by several different instruments on a single tune. The project also represents a great spirit of cooperation and diversity of language, culture, age, and gender. It includes the inputs of musical legends, seasoned pros, and amateurs. The wonderfully rich and often stereotyped musical cultures of both Mexico and Hawaii are represented here with the authenticity of lived experience.
Adios Ke Aloha: Waves of the Same Sea
is a worthy addition to Los Cenzontles� important work. Quoting Rodriguez again, �Culture is a fabric within which we are all woven.�

items.body:
The musical partnership between Kalaniemi and Alakotila has thrived over a remarkable 35 years, long enough to the Finnish pair to develop a stunning intimacy and telepathy. Kalaniemi is a lovingly melodic accordion player, with a sharp ear for a good tune, building each one into a thing of great beauty, while pianist Alakotila not only supports her but adds enough of his own to help transform every piece into a glistening gem.
There�s a sense of calmness to the work here, a long, sweet exhalation between two instrumentalists who are deep enough in sync to allow seamless improvisation beyond any written score and carry the listeners along with them. For much of the album, it�s just the pair of them, including Kalaniemi�s wordless voice, as on the opener, the tradional �Lyck�nskan.� She does charmingly sing lyrics on the title track, written by Lasse M�rtenson, with the sound there neatly and sparingly expanded with the addition of a string quartet.
Morgondimma
There are several original pieces alongside the tradition, with Kalaniemi�s �Hambo Vid F�bodan� a real standout, and it�s perhaps inevitable on any disc featuring accordion that a Piazzolla tune should be included, brings its own shadows to the whole (�Oblivion�). And, this being Finland, a tango is almost obligatory, in this case Alakotila�s �Tango Berlin.�
Tango Berlin
There�s a gentle, dreamlike quality to so much of this, flowing and mellifluous. The pieces aren�t an arena for showy virtuosity. Instead, the two musicians serve the tune, exploring and genuinely enjoying their performances.
It won�t shake the earth, but it makes for some true listening beauty.

items.body:
Sometime in 1986, perhaps in a Paris caf�, Dominique Cravic, a singer, guitarist, and musical archivist, met Robert Crumb, an underground cartoonist, banjo and mandolin player, and jug-band aficionado. Over a few glasses of marc, to continue to speculate, they conjured up the idea for Les Primitifs du futur.  Since then, they have recorded an impossible-to-categorize series of albums, with cover illustrations by Crumb, of which Les Crimes du Mussette is the fifth.
Weird and wonderful, it sounds like they rooted through an attic full of 78 RPM records, scribbled down some arrangements, and then played them on a collection of instruments they found in another attic, including accordion, sax, xylophone, clarinet, banjo, ukulele, theremin, Hawaiian guitar, bagpipe chanter (I�m guessing here), and musical saw.
Ne tirez pas sur le pianiste (excerpt)
The 27 short tracks are mostly voiced by Cravic, who talk-sings in the manner of an everyman Maurice Chevalier. He is often accompanied by the accordion, a customary instrument in the bal-musette style that remains a strong element of the eclectic range of styles they have managed to synthesize. They also include ragtime, jug, French chanson, and, to my ears, skiffle,  just to get the list started.
Ukulele Lady (excerpt)
The liner notes point out that �Les Crimes du Musette is also a gold mine for scholars, a veritable treasure trove.� Exploring the treasures is beyond my scope here, as each tune has a long history. A highlight for me is the humorous �Ukulele Lady� from 1925, which first delighted me on Arlo Guthrie�s 1971 album
Hobo�s Lullaby
. The song has also been covered by Bing Crosby, Peter Sellers, and Bette Midler.
N'oublie pas Gr�co (excerpt)
A more serious item is �N�oublie pas Gr�co� (Don�t Forget Gr�co�)  is a tribute to the legendary chanteuse and heroine of the French Resistance, Juliette Gr�co, who died in 2020. You will also hear old chestnuts like �Fum�e aux yeux� (�Smoke Gets in Your Eyes�),  �Boude pas� (�Take Five�), and �Prive d�amour� (�As Time Goes By�).
This record is a curiosity, but it is performed by serious musicians with total commitment. In this, I was reminded of the similarly indefinable Dan Hicks & the Hot Licks. Long-forgotten music and abandoned styles are given new animation with obvious enthusiasm and care. Speaking about himself and his collaborators, many of whom are in their seventies, Dominique Cravic says, �The young have fire, but we have light.� In its own little corner,
Les Crimes du Musette
shines bright.

items.body:
A debut, digital-only EP from a Danish trio, led by one of the Nordic folk scene�s outstanding and experienced vocalists, Mia Guldhammer. Five tracks, with the musicians bringing their own perspectives to mostly traditional music. There�s a lovely ancient, creaky mood throughout.
The opener, �Svennedal,� with its rough, cantering rhythm, offers a perfect shop window for Guldhammer�s impressive, persuasive voice, while jaw harp and bagpipes bring an insistent propulsion to �Nordg�rd,� the only original here, by band member Morten Musicus.
Cimbalom adds a delicate backdrop to the traditional �Agnete Of Bjergmanden,� with Guldhammer�s soft jaw harp offering extra textures to the other instruments, as it brings a springy opening to the final cut, �Orms�,� mingling with flute and strings to create something quite thrilling and off kilter on this instrumental.
Five tracks, and an introduction to a band that already seems very mature and accomplished. A strong beginning � what will GuldGanger do with an entire album?
items.label: Go' Danish Folk Music
items._cn_summary: 这是一张丹麦三人组的数字EP，由北欧民谣界经验丰富的歌手Mia Guldhammer领衔，五首作品大多基于传统曲调，却以现代个人视角重新演绎。整体氛围古老而略带粗粝，开场曲《Svennedal》以跳跃的节奏展现歌者富有说服力的嗓音，口弦与风笛的叠加为《Nordgård》注入持续推动力。钦巴龙在《Agnete Af Bjergmanden》中构成细腻底色，而器乐曲《Ormsø》通过口弦、长笛与弦乐的混合制造出失衡而迷人的声响。乐队虽是新面孔，但表现成熟，音乐既保留北欧民间叙事的原始质感，又通过非常规音色组合制造出微妙的实验感，值得关注。

items._cn_summary: 面影ラッキーホール（おもかげラッキーホール）的《代理母》与《音楽ぎらい》两张专辑将以彩色黑胶形式在2026年10月由Tower Records限定再版，附赠aCKy与sinner-yang对谈的特别乐评内页。小林私以个人视角回忆初次接触《代理母》中「今夜、巣鴨で」的经历，被封面、专辑名与曲名整体氛围吸引，开篇即被爆炸般的吉他段落抓住。歌词层面，小林私指出该乐队在词汇与意象的「罗列」与「搭配」上具有非常规的组合方式，文本呈现出异常而独特的美学张力。文章属于专辑再版纪念的特别寄稿，侧重于听者个人感受与歌词文字分析，对音乐本身的编曲、制作层面着墨有限。整体定位偏向另类摇滚范畴，与实验、前卫、爵士或电子等核心偏好存在距离，但其歌词的文学性与非常规意象处理具有一定的前卫色彩。

items.album: ZeroMoon Selects the Best of Bandcamp for August 2026
items.excerpt: Washington, D.C. experimental label ZeroMoon has published its Best of August 2026 playlist, a seven-track, 66-minute survey of “obscure, obtuse, and overlooked” releases. The set moves through drone, noise, free improvisation, electroacoustic music, and other experimental territory, with selections from Šimanský Vaľko Podracký, Cedrik Fermont, Diurnal Burdens, Tim Olive, Gentle Fire, Irene Aranda, and LULE.

items.body: Review by siLLy puPPy — This short-lived mysterious act that emerged from Pushkin, a nearby suburb of St Petersburg, Russiais the epitome of obscurity having only released its sole effort Литургия безумия / A LITURGY OFMADNESS in 1991 and then never to be heard from again. Given it debuted during the tumultuous timewhen the Soviet Union was collapsing into the Russian Federation and outlying nations, the band andalbum has become a very forgotten entry in the region's rich musical history. This psychedelicprogressive band was the trio of bassist Aleksandr Berezkin, guitarist Aleksey Romanov and drummerIvan Fedenko, the latter of which was a seasoned Soviet musician having played in the new wave actAVIA as well as the jazz fusion ensemble Junglie.Together this triumvirate of instrumental experimental prog crafted an album's worth of complexpsychedelia where classic prog nods effortlessly free flow through an album's worth of psychedelichaze augmented by Beefheart inspired angularities and Pink Floyd infused grooviness. Whiletechnically hosting 13 individual tracks, the album can rightfully be thought of as two side-longtracks that offer variations on a theme to transition from one motif and cadence to the nextoffering moments of high energy rock along with an ever-changing rotisserie of time signatures,tempos, tones and progressive weavings. The album has been cited as catering the melodic prowess ofclassic Yes recordings laced with off-kilter avant-progeny angularities that sprang into existenceat the end of the 1970s but this is very subtle in actuality.Beginning with the raucous ride that constitutes side one, the wily suite "Бешеный Огурец, Часть 1 /Mad Cucumber, Part" displays a fertile musical fecundity in action where essentially a jam bandchannels its inner prog credentials and takes a five-part journey through musical terrains thatemulate past masters but yet sound like none of them. A crafty and creative wild ride through mostlyguitar-driven / keyboard-free excursions through meandering musical motifs, A LITURGY OF MADNESSdespite it's title and insinuations that it will be a dark journey of the soul actually comes off asmore light-hearted and stews in the broth of psychedelia more than the underbelly of the earlyUnivers Zero playbook yet many nods to avant-prog masters of yore insert their angular angles intothe overall context. Some clear King Crimson references also are in the overall fabric.Although some will claim the album is a continuous flow from beginning to end, in reality the firstside is clearly delineated from the second with "Бешеный Огурец, Часть 2 / Mad Cucumber, Part 2"taking on a distinctly different mood setting although in general the same meandering unpredictableprocession of what sounds like aimless musically lollygagging that somehow flows organically andwithout startling unrelated transitions. Despite the avant-prog reference the music is overall moreon the melodic side but creatively distinct as not really pointing to many other bands that hademerged up to this point in the prog timeline. For the most part this is a subtle release thatdoesn't offer a lot in terms of timbres and instrumental offerings with all the creative effortstucked into the varying motifs that span on for a 40 1/2 minute mind journey. This is one that tooka few spins to sink in but ultimately delivers a nice meandering package of highly idiosyncraticpsychedelia that sounds fairly unique.
items._genre: psychedelic rock / progressive rock / experimental rock
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑来自俄罗斯圣彼得堡附近普希金城的一支神秘短命乐队，1991年苏联解体动荡时期发行，是该乐队唯一作品，后再无音讯。乐队为三人编制，贝斯手、吉他手与鼓手，鼓手曾有苏联新浪潮与爵士融合乐团的经历。整张专辑以迷幻前卫摇滚为主轴，融合了King Crimson式棱角、Yes式旋律铺陈、Pink Floyd式律动以及Beefheart式的扭曲切分。十三首曲目实际可视为两张长篇大块，吉他驱动的无键盘即兴段落贯穿其中，频繁变换拍号、速度与音色，在迷幻氛围中穿行。前卫摇滚的实验性结构与迷幻层次感是这张专辑的核心特质，对前卫/迷幻交叉地带有兴趣的听众值得关注。

items.body: Review by Hector Enrique — Led by its frontman and multi-instrumentalist, Christofer Johnsson, Therion dedicates "Secret of the Runes" (2001), its tenth album, to exploring the mysteries of Yggdrasil: the enormous sacred tree that occupies a central place in the Norse worldview and around which the nine worlds are arranged. The concept is rooted in the fascinating Norse mythology, as transmitted by medieval sources that preserve much older traditions. An album shrouded in the misty, mystical, and legendary aura inspired by gods, giants, humans, and elves, it is grounded in symphonic metal with a distinct neoclassical element and serves as a starting point for delving into the various branches of the metal genre found within the Swedes' broad and shadowy sonic spectrum.Thus, the intricate choral, orchestral, and operatic arrangements of the thirty or so guest musicians blend harmoniously with Kristian Niemann's powerful and sophisticated guitar riffs and solos, both in the death metal elements of the majestic "Ginnungagap" -which opens the way to the chaos of the primordial void of creation and is surely one of the album's best tracks- as well as in the depths of the doom-laden "Jotunheim," the black-metal darkness of the lugubrious "Nifelheim" and "Helheim," and the power-metal-style bursts of energy in the fast-paced "Asgard" and "Muspelheim."And that sense of persistent tension and chaos conveyed by the most extreme and dense tracks finds gradations in the more progressive "Schwarzalbenheim" and a breath of fresh air both in the serene "Midgard" - which refers to the realm of humans and is another of the album's major themes - and in the folk-metal interludes of the celestial "Ljusalfheim" and the pastoral "Vanaheim." All of this comes together to form an album with a wide range of nuances that mesh seamlessly, which the title track "Secret of the Runes" sums up as an operatic compendium and a very fitting concluding epilogue.An excellent album that, along with "Theli" (1996) and "Vovin" (1998), represents one of the highest peaks of compositional and musical maturity in the band's entire career, as well as establishing itself as a cornerstone of symphonic metal.4 stars
items._cn_summary: Therion的第十张专辑以北欧神话中世界树尤克特拉希尔为核心概念，构建了一张融合交响、合唱、歌剧与金属元素的宏大叙事。九首作品分别对应九大世界，从混沌虚空Ginnungagap的死亡金属，到Jotunheim的厄运金属沉重，再到Nifelheim与Helheim的黑金属阴郁，以及Asgard的力量金属激昂，呈现出风格谱系的纵深。Niemann的吉他riff与独奏在繁复管弦乐编配中保持辨识度，Ljusalfheim的民谣间奏与Midgard的宁静段落提供了情绪喘息空间。结尾同名曲以歌剧式总结呼应整张专辑的仪式感。该评论信息详实，将此作定位为乐队创作成熟期的高峰之一，与Theli、Vovin并列。

items.body: Review by kenethlevine — While one can never accuse JOANNA NEWSOM of adopting conventional voice and arrangements on a path to surprisingly broad cult acceptance, "Divers", still her most recent, is refreshingly accessible in both arenas. While she has retained her core idiosyncrasies, since "Have one on Me" her retooled pipes, emphasis on more conventional song structures and reliance on a more expansive instrumental palette have allowed what was always there to emerge more plainly, from the Celtic harp inspirations to the Appalachian allusions, and, yes, a little bit country. The centerpiece title cut argues best for this successful evolution in a progressive context, beginning with her unabashed plucked intro and mysterious airs, while "Leaving the City" among others sports her evolution into rapid-fire meters, even if the end of the closer is an overly over the top example. Other standouts are the earthier "The Things I say" and "Same Old Man", the earworm "You will not take my heart alive", and especially "A Pin-Light Bent", which sounds like Joanna guesting on an early IAMTHEMORNING number, that is, sublime.While Joanna isn't ever for the musically unadventurous chart gazers, "Divers" is probably the best place to get your feet wet before plunging deeper with abandon, an activity I fully endorse.
items._genre: prog folk / art pop / chamber folk
items._cn_summary: Joanna Newsom的《Divers》在前卫民谣框架内展现了声音设计的独特性：凯尔特竖琴的灵感贯穿全作，辅以阿巴拉契亚民谣暗示和乡村音乐色彩，编曲层次丰富。标题曲以拨弦前奏和神秘氛围开场，尾曲则在快速变换的节拍中呈现复杂结构。歌词层面保留了她标志性的怪异性，但人声处理和器乐编排更加内敛克制。制作上融合了室内乐编制与现代民谣元素，多首曲目展现出旋律记忆点与编排深度的平衡。作为她最具可接近性的作品，它为听众提供了进入她更极端创作领域的入口，同时也保持了足够的艺术独特性。

items.body: Review by tupan — I am not much of a review guy, but after listening to the fourth VISCERA/// album several times, I think I need to give my two cents! VISCERA/// (yep, the three slashes are part of the name) is a italian band that began its career playing grindcore/goregrind in the early 00's, but soon moving to atmospheric sludge in their debut. This one is their fourth full lenght (don't counting two collaboration albums), and was released this year by Time to Kill Records. The music is a refreshing mix of atmo sludge, grunge, prog and many nods to post-punk from the eighties. The vocals change from harsh black metal shrieks to clean Jaz Coleman (from KILLING JOKE fame) inspired singing! I really recommend this album, one of the best surprises of 2026. Check it out!

items.body: Northern Irish composer Hannah Peel will release her original score for “Underland” on CD on 16 October via Rivertones, followed by a world premiere performance of the score at the Barbican on 24 October as part of the “Hannah Peel: In Focus” two-day series. “Underland” is Peel’s score for Robert Petit’s film adaptation of Robert Macfarlane’s book of the same name. The album combines synthesizers with ancient Mayan pod trumpets and an Iron Age horn called a carnyx, alongside baroque choir and string orchestra. Peel said she read Macfarlane’s book in 2019 and had already used some of its words on her 2022 album “The Unfolding,” calling the chance to score the film itself “beautiful synchronicity.” She described the project as scoring for “these astronauts of the underworld, those sacred ancient cave systems,” and said combining “mythology, technology and possibility” was central to the record. The CD tracklist runs 18 tracks, including “Into the Underland,” “Xibalba,” “Seeing in the Dark,” “The Waiting Wonder,” “You Don’t See Sunlight,” “The Earth Doesn’t Forget,” and “The Ascent.” The Barbican premiere, adapted for stage by Kieran Brunt, will be performed by contemporary vocal ensemble Shards with imagery from the film adapted by director Robert Petit. It forms the second half of “Hannah Peel: In Focus,” which opens on 23 October at Milton Court with “PIA,” a new live production of her 2020 album “Mary Casio: Journey to Cassiopeia,” created with choreographer Katya Bourvis and creative producer Tala Lee-Turton and scored for a 17-piece brass band. The 24 October date also includes a performance of “The Endless Dance,” Peel’s recent album with percussionist Beibei Wang on Real World Recordings. Peel and Beibei Wang will also play the Glasshouse International Centre for Music in Gateshead on 20 October and St Luke’s in Glasgow on 21 October. About Hannah Peel Hannah Peel is a Northern Irish composer, producer, and broadcaster whose work often connects science and music. Her studio albums include “Mary Casio: Journey to Cassiopeia” (2017), scored for synthesizers and colliery brass band; the Mercury Prize-nominated “Fir Wave” (2021); “The Unfolding” (2022) featuring the Paraorchestra; and “The Endless Dance” (2026) with Beibei Wang. Peel received an Emmy nomination for her score on “Game of Thrones: The Last Watch” and has since scored “Scoop” (Netflix), “Bring Them Down” (Mubi), “Midwinter Break” (Focus Features), and the horror film “Saccharine.” Her electronic score for “The Midwich Cuckoos” (Sky) won the Ivor Novello Award for Best Television Soundtrack in 2023, making her the first solo female composer to win that award. Peel also presents BBC Radio 3’s “Night Tracks.” “Underland” continues her run of film and stage work, following its “beautiful synchronicity” with a book she had already drawn on for “The Unfolding.” You Don’t See Sunlight by Hannah Peel

items._cn_summary: 北爱尔兰作曲家Hannah Peel为Robert Macfarlane同名著作的电影改编版本创作原创配乐，专辑融合合成器、古玛雅豆号与铁器时代的角号carnyx，搭配巴洛克合唱团与弦乐编制。她将古老神话叙事与电子音色结合，灵感源自洞穴这一人类原始空间的意象。配乐包含十八首曲目，从《Into the Underland》到《The Ascent》构建出完整的地下世界声景。专辑由Rivertones厂牌发行CD，随后将在Barbican进行世界首演，由当代声乐团体Shards演绎，舞台改编由Kieran Brunt完成。该作品延续了她在科学、神话与音乐之间建立联系的创作脉络，与之前水星奖提名专辑及艾美奖提名配乐一脉相承。

items.body: Tout Debord release “Necrologia”, a 32-track double CD compilation, on Icy Cold Records. The digipak gathers the complete collection of EPs and singles the project released between 2021 and 2026, on labels including Detriti Records, Sierpien Records and Salle d’Attente. Tout Debord is the solo project of Leonid Diaghilev, born in Belarus and based in Paris for several years, who wrote, recorded and mixed every song on “Necrologia” himself. The compilation moves from 80s-inspired coldwave to synthpunk influences drawn from the 2000s, filtered through a lo-fi aesthetic across two discs of sixteen tracks each. A vinyl edition with a shorter tracklist is planned for later in the year. About Tout Debord Tout Debord is the solo project of Leonid Diaghilev, a musician born in Belarus and based in Paris, France. The project’s name fuses the French phrase “tout d’abord” (“first of all”) with a nod to philosopher and Situationist Guy Debord. Since starting the project in Paris in 2020, Diaghilev has released a string of EPs and singles across several independent labels, drawing on the early albums of The Cure and industrial synthpop acts such as Fad Gadget and Depeche Mode, alongside the French cold wave scene of the 1980s. “Necrologia”, released through Icy Cold Records, collects that catalogue on a single double-disc release for the first time.
items._cn_summary: Tout Debord 是白俄罗斯裔巴黎音乐人 Leonid Diaghilev 的单人项目，2020年成立以来陆续在 Detriti Records、Sierpien Records 等独立厂牌发行了多张 EP 与单曲。《Necrologia》由 Icy Cold Records 以双 CD 形式集结了 2021 至 2026 年间的全部作品，共 32 首。音乐风格跨越八十年代冷潮与千禧年合成器朋克的影响，辅以低保真美学过滤。The Cure 早期作品、Fad Gadget 与 Depeche Mode 的工业合成器流行，以及法国八十年代冷潮场景构成其创作参照。所有曲目均由 Diaghilev 独立完成词曲、录制与混音，年底还将推出曲目较少的黑胶版本。

items.body: Dungeon synth, the offspring of '90s black metal and ambient music, is a lo-fi genre with a focus on fantastical settings and sonic themes. Ambient music is exactly how it sounds and needs no in-depth explanation for music enthusiasts, and the same attitude extends to the 1990s concrete wave of black metal. Comfy synth, one of numerous prefix-synth sister genres, concentrates on sentimentality and nostalgic sounds; a comfy atmosphere with finite overlap with metal. Comfy synth is a relatively new style, rising in the late 2010s—arguably with Grandma's Cottage's self-titled record, released in December 2019—while dungeon synth falls many decades back. The man behind Hole Dweller, Tim Rowland is a true synth pioneer. Situated in Atlanta, he brought dungeon-infused comfy synth to the ([extremely] relative) mainstream with 2019's Flies the Coop, completing a trilogy started in 2024. His most recent album, Long Road Home, caught my eye this week—mostly through the album art, but partially because of the online hubbub surrounding it. At a digestible half-hour runtime, it isn't a daunting introduction to the genre. Each of the fourteen tracks spans no longer than two minutes (the longest, "stay while the birds sing," reaches 2:47, while "painted in memory" only runs to 1:33), and this is on purpose: Rowland focuses on minimalism, and each track can be looped, like video game soundtracks. Other instruments, like a stringed folk guitar of sorts, are welcome, frequenting tracks with rain and/or nature sounds. The darkest highlight is "bones consumed by moss and root," which takes a badass title and turns the mood to melancholic instead of hopeful. That being said, there are some instances where the focus is taken slightly away from the pure ambience that Hole Dweller convinced me to love in just one playthrough. One is the soft percussion in "summer inventory," and while a steady beat isn't an awful inclusion, the song following it, "sleeping fields," exemplifies that soft cinematics are better on their own, and "in the afterglow" follows this trend. The only other gripe I have is the shift from lo-fi to modern production means. The LP's overall quality dips during "grace in low places" and "in the afterglow", and—despite it being in dungeon synth's nature to not sound crystal clear—the bulk of Long Road Home seems very present-day. This isn't even a complaint though, really, since this duality of feels is perfect for introductory dungeon synthers. Personally, I need no further convincing to join Hole Dweller on the Long Road Home. Long Road Home by Hole Dweller

items._cn_summary: Hole Dweller 的《Long Road Home》以半小时篇幅呈现十四首短曲，每首不超过三分钟，可循环播放，呼应电子游戏配乐传统。作品以极简主义手法构建氛围，合成器音色为核心，辅以民谣吉他与雨声自然采样。评论指出专辑整体保持低保真质感，但部分曲目如《grace in low places》和《in the afterglow》转向现代制作手段，使整体听感略显割裂。打击乐的加入也被认为略显多余。亮点在于《bones consumed by moss and root》，标题暗示沉重情绪，实际却走向忧郁内省。作为舒适合成器的代表，Hole Dweller 将地牢合成器与怀旧情感融合，为入门听众提供友好路径，专辑在氛围营造上扎实，但跨界融合与实验性较为有限。

items.body: Label: Sunnyside Records, 2026 Personnel - Lucian Ban: piano; Abraham Burton: tenor saxophone; John Hébert: bass; Eric McPherson: drums; Gavril Tarmure: vocals (#9). Romanian-born pianist and composer Lucian Ban returns with Rush , a refreshingly vital album from his acclaimed group Elevation, featuring saxophonist Abraham Burton, bassist John Hébert, and drummer Eric McPherson. The inspirations come from many sides. The opener, " Dark Blue ”, is a dedication to pianist Abdullah Ibrahim — velvety, comforting contemporary jazz that revels in modal sophistication within an aesthetic that seems to intersect Mingus's ballads and Motian's soft lyric abstraction. Burton speaks wonders here, and I'm especially fond of the way Ban solos, using splendorous harmonic manifestations to accompany himself. " Serenade For Andrew " is a tribute to another great pianist, the inimitable Andrew Hill. Delivered in 3/4, this is solid post-bop with depth, a strong emotional center, and reverence for the man to whom this gripping composition is dedicated. " Christine's Hope " is an Americana-tinged ballad, but the mood lifts with “ Rush ", whose traditionally lilting locomotion, cubist accentuations, imposing pedal points, and rhythmic complexity conjure an amalgamation of Thelonious Monk, Herbie Nichols, Charlie Parker, and Sam Rivers. " Congestion Tax ", improvised spontaneously by the quartet, gradually lends the music its combustive edge, while the delicate " Chakra ", written for Billy Strayhorn, seems to find some solace in Yusef Lateef's Eastern moods. The music is permeated with interplay, sometimes leading to mesmerizing results, as in “Elevation", an achingly beautiful and leisurely illuminated ballad composed for Larry Willis, where the quartet showcases razor-sharp musicianship, sophistication, and passion for sound. Hébert's intimate lyricism is featured here, and the group's spotless dynamics leave us in awe. The journey wraps up with " Golden Oriole ”, a traditional folk song featuring Romanian singer Gavril Tarmure, whose genuine feeling is immediately apparent. He had collaborated with Ban on three folk-jazz crossover pieces included on Songs From Afar (Sunnyside, 2016). These tautly arranged compositions are given fascinating colors, shades, and directions under the captivating performance of Ban's Elevation. Favorite Tracks: 01 - Dark Blue ► 04 - Rush ► 05 - Elevation ► 07 - Chakra

items._cn_summary: 罗马尼亚钢琴家Lucian Ban携Elevation乐队带来新专辑《Rush》，整体延续后波普爵士脉络，同时融入民谣元素。乐队编制为钢琴、四重奏加特邀人声，作品向多位钢琴大师致敬：开篇'Dark Blue'致敬Abdullah Ibrahim，走modal路线，旋律温和饱满；'Serenade For Andrew'以3/4拍致敬Andrew Hill，沉稳而有情感重量；同名曲'Rush'融合Monk式的立体切分与节奏复杂性，将多重视角编织在一起。'Congestion Tax'为四重奏即兴作品，燃烧感强烈；'Chakra'面向Billy Strayhorn，呈现东方冥想气质。终曲'Golden Oriole'为罗马尼亚民谣，与人声合作，是爵士与东欧民间素材的交汇点。整张专辑在致敬传统的同时展现出乐队成员间紧密的互动，乐手各自的抒情性与动态控制为作品提供了层次。

For example, Slovenian-native R�n�lius Bikar�s searing violin opens the set with �R�fuge.� He and his self-named ensemble channel pan-European Roma history.
Meanwhile, �Poor Boy� is a Django Reinhardt-inspired swing tune by Charlotte Pelgen & Bipolar Bows. Pelgen sings in English, and with her ukulele strumming sounding very much like a tenor banjo, the tune is enlivened by Lotte Remmen�s St�phane Grappelli-like fiddle lines.
The distinctive sound of the oud announces yet another musical tradition. Blending Mediterranean with Arabic sounds, the Lebanese-Belgian singer Amber Haddad and her trio, oudist Adil Benhsain and double bassist Martijn Vanbuel, spin a beguiling musical web. According to the liner notes (translated from the Dutch), �Tawazden� is about �seeking balance and finding peace within a complex environment.� Further, �the various spaces of the abbey and their murals are the direct source of inspiration.�
The accordion is especially prominent. So too is the Western classical tradition. Sounding almost Baroque, �Sacristia Invisibilis,� is another standout for me. Here, mandolinist Andries Boone is joined by Anouk Sanczuk on octave violin (sometimes called the baritone violin, tuned an octave lower than standard) and on harpsichord Sandra Van der Gucht. They create an indescribable sound you have to hear.
Throughout, the Abbey�s stone presence looms. Aur�lie Charneux�s solo clarinet piece �L'Ape Millenaria� is about a thousand-year-old bee that haunts the abbey. �Thila,� by Enara Navaira, evokes ancient Celts with a jazzy double bass and drum kit behind throat singing and Citera (a kind of Hungarian zither).
Airboxes is a duo who mix chromatic and diatonic accordions. Their offering �Abdij 1� sounds improvised. Again from the liner notes, �they share their impressions of the timelessness of monastic life.�
Despite the wide range of styles,
The Sound of the Abbey
has a coherence, perhaps informed by the artists� shared inspiration. The record is often surprising and always soothing. Three years in the making, the ensembles were lovingly recorded and mixed by Bert Huysentruyt and mastered by Pieter De Wagter from Equus Mastering. They have rendered a warm sound using the natural reverb of ancient stone provided by the project�s silent partner.

I went to Kyiv to see them at the time of the Maidan protests, just after the shooting by snipers of over a hundred protesters. I intentionally didn�t read this album�s booklet notes before listening, so that I could react to it without sympathetic pre-judgement, just as music. It�s strong musically and vocally by any standards, Ukrainian or otherwise. When I did then turn to the notes that translate and explain the songs, I had that rare experience, for me, of becoming moist-eyed. The songs are a mix of traditional and original. They are focused on the abduction by Russia of about 20,000 Ukrainian children who have been taken from their parents in Russian-occupied eastern Ukraine and sent to Russia, in an attempt to turn them into haters of their native land and people. It�s a heinous war crime. Marichka is a Ukrainian-Canadian singer who moves between Canada and her homeland. For this album she�s gathered two groups of musicians, one in each country. Both ensembles contribute vocals and instrumentation, mostly bowed strings, plus some bandura and piano. The group in Ukraine includes Lisa from the destroyed and invaded city of Mariupol, playing a solo on double ocarina; at 16 she was one of the stolen children but managed to return to Ukraine. Daughters of Donbas � co-led by Marichka and singer/bandurist Alina Kuzma, who shares the lead vocal role � is an all-female ensemble in Canada that tours performing these songs. �Foreign Land� is a reworking of a traditional song about the young girls who were sent away to work in foreign households - Marichka�s grandmother was one of these - that can also be taken to refer to the plight of today�s stolen children. The translation goes: A mother packed up her daughter To leave for a strange land To a strange land with strange people Oh, who will pity you, my daughter? Those who will beat me will pity me I'll never again live with you, my mother When, my daughter, should I expect you to come home? When the grass in the garden grows, my mother The grass grew and grew and began to dry The mother was waiting for her daughter to return, and began to cry Did you hear, my mother, how I came to you? How I flew as a bird above your window? How I cooed like a dove? If, my daughter, I could hear you I would open all the doors and windows To let you fly in Songs of Stolen Children by Daughters of Donbas, Alina Kuzma, Zo� Santo As befits the song, Marichka�s vocal here is gentle. But in the second track, �Rusalka,� with Alina Kuzma taking the lead vocals, things turn harsh and fierce. A rusalka is a mythical creature, a nature spirit of fields, forest and rivers, that features in traditional ritual songs. The melody of this one is by Zo� Santo and Kuzma, with lyrics drawing on tradition and the composition of Santo and 19thC Ukrainian poet and folklorist Taras Shevchenko. An ominous double-bass drone, chunking strings, a slithering vocal that moves into sections of white-voice fast recitative and expands into a soaring wild cry. The lyrics are very dark, perhaps evoking the hell of the front line: Home a hell of old growth stumps Marsh a mud of memories Don�t get bogged down in these parts Your kind won�t last a day in here While witches still fly, while roosters have yet to crow, Come here, something arises, �neath the oak something walks. A rusalka sat on a white birch, rusalky asked girls for shirts. Long fingers and nails so sharp Tongue forked round serrated teeth Moss grows down beneath her parts Weeds braided from ear to ear While witches still fly, while roosters have yet to crow, Come here, something arises, �neath the oak something walks. �Girls, my friends, give me your shirts. Though I�m thin, give me a thin one.� Here live us the backless ones Many voices of dead sons You are right to quake in fear Send your sinful children here �Who Am I� is a plea of separation and disorientation, the pain and confusion of an abducted child, contrasting �the human in me� and �the creature in me,� like an internalized riddle-song, with the refrain, in English: Who am I for you? Who am I for me? Do you know me? Really know me? �Enchantress,� passionately sung by Kuzma to her own bandura accompaniment, a girl�s lament of the loss of her brave love taken from her by the enchantress, who is an allegory of war, is based on a traditional song and uses that style of melody and lyrics, �Riddle,� sung by Marichka, reworks a traditional riddle song to be the riddles told by the grandfather of a child, 12-year-old Kira from Mariupol, who experienced the death of her father and her abduction to Russia. Her grandfather tracked her down, and brought her back, traumatized, and asked her riddles - as the notes say �to jog her memory, and remind her who she was, where her home was, and of her family�s love for her.� Songs of Stolen Children by Daughters of Donbas, Marichka �4.5.0� is a military expression for �all�s well� or �all is quiet.� The song is a message, as from a mother, to a stolen child. Marichka�s voice is cherishing: Remember this: I am with you, I am here Don't give up, I'm with you. Don't give up, I'm with you Your hope is my weapon Don't be sad, I'm with you 4.5.0. will be again �breaking into a tearing howl: And when the world's axis breaks When the sky folds like a parchment Out of nowhere her words will come� �and back to fragile reassurance �It's all right, I'm here, I'm here� "Lullaby," based on a traditional lullaby, sung by Alina Kuzma to accompaniment by her bandura and Zo� Santo's viola, starts in gentle lullaby style, but moves to a lament; it's for the stolen children and those who, as the notes put it, 'have been stolen for ever.' Songs of Stolen Children by Daughters of Donbas, Marichka �Remember, I Believe in You� is a powerful piece of harmonizing vocals and slithering strings. Here�s the story it�s based on: Yevhen lived in Mariupol with his three young children. During the siege they lived in a basement bomb shelter for months. One day, Russian soldiers entered their bomb shelter. Yevhen was taken to a filtration camp and separated from his children who were all taken to a hospital and then to Russian summer �camp�. In the filtration camp Yevhen was brutally tortured and forced to sleep standing on one leg. He tried to fall asleep, whispering prayers for his children: �Everything will be fine, I believe in you.� After his release he walked 30 kilometers to the place where his children had been taken but it was too late. They had already been sent to Moscow. Yevhen learned of this after receiving a text from one of his children who had found an unattended device. He traveled thousands of kilometers, crossed the borders of three countries, endured checks, interrogations and danger to reach Moscow and take his children home. All those days he tirelessly repeated to himself, �I believe in myself, I believe in my kids. Everything will be good.� �Another Heaven,� sung by Marichka with the ensemble in Ukraine, is inspired by another heart-rending story: Ilya was 9 years old when his mother was killed by a rocket strike right in front of him. He was taken to a hospital in occupied Donetsk, where 15 pieces of shrapnel were removed from his body without anesthesia. After he appeared in a report on Russian television, Ilya�s grandmother learned his location. She managed to bring her grandson to Kyiv, where he lives now, experiencing missile attacks every night. At age 11, he says that it is up to everyone to fight enemies, to protect other cities, and to build another heaven, where your home will not be destroyed. In 2014, during the Kyiv Maidan protests, Marichka wrote and performed �Red Boots Tango,� using a melody she�d put to a poem by Taras Shevchenko. For this album she sings it again in Ukraine, with the ensemble there adding swirling, classic tango-style strings. Songs of Stolen Children by Daughters of Donbas, BanduraGirl The final track on the album is a solo, recorded in Kyiv, by Anastasiya Voytyuk, accompanying herself on the older, simpler form of bandura that was used by kobzars to accompany epic poetry, and also on the nowadays more well-known big, heavy form developed from it in Soviet times that was made mainly in the piano factory at Chernihiv. Her song, �Soon I Will Be Back,� is based on a poem by novelist, journalist and war crime researcher Victoria Amelia, who was killed in 2023, in the city of Kramatorsk in Donbas, by a Russian rocket. Find the artist online. Further reading: Otava Yo - Do You Love (Review) Sofia Rei - Umbral (Review)

items._cn_summary: 这张专辑聚焦于乌克兰被占领土上约两万儿童被俄罗斯强行带走的战争罪行主题，将传统民歌与原创作品交织。由乌克兰裔加拿大歌手Marichka与班杜拉手Alina Kuzma联合领导的全女性团体Daughters of Donbas演绎，音乐以弓弦乐器为核心，搭配班杜拉、钢琴乃至双陶笛等音色。曲目《Foreign Land》以传统旋律诉说被送往异乡劳作的少女命运，歌词在母女对话中展开悲伤叙事，呼应当下离散儿童的处境，Marichka的演唱温柔克制。另一首《Rusalka》则由Alina Kuzma主唱，取材自斯拉夫民间传说中的田野与河流精灵，音乐转向激烈粗粝，与前曲形成强烈反差。专辑横跨加拿大与乌克兰两地的音乐人合作录制，展现了乌克兰传统音乐在当代语境下的延续与抗争。

items.body: Review by siLLy puPPy — In many ways the Russian modern day equivalent of Goblin, the Vladimir (city) based ENINE has carvedout a unique niche in the world of symphonic guitar-driven prog that takes inspiration thematicallyfrom the subject matter of early silent films, patricianly the horror cinema of the 1920s whilemarrying it to the world of 70s symphonic and space rock prog courtesy of bands such as Eloy, PinkFloyd, Camel and Genesis. This band was founded by guitarist Vladimir Mihailov and keyboardist IlyaFrolov who worked together in the prog band Algabas and after adding three more members released alive album "Live In Saint Petersburg" which served as the official debut. This first studio offeringTHE GREAT SILENT followed in 2018 and to this day only one additional album, "Spiritus Natura" hascome to fruition.Living up to the album title, the subject matter is indeed silent horror and sci-fi films thatspanned the 1910s and 1920s. Inspirations are drawn from classics such as "Metropolis (1927)" and"Noseferatu (1922)" as well as "Dr. Caligari (1920)" and "Frankenstein (1910)" all without reallytaking the music into the dark mood settings that such titles would suggest. This all instrumentalalbum features eight tracks (2 of which are lesss than a minute) and offers some nice symphonicspace jamming with some sounding fairly original and others sounding right out of the 70s playbook."Waiting For.." offers a cliche throwback to 70s Pink Floyd for example. The opening "Welcome ToMonochrome" sets the tone for a nonchalant ride through jammy space rock laced with symphonicbombast reminiscent most of 70s Eloy yet the band steers clear of repeating the same idea for toolong. The strongest tracks come at the beginning with "The Curse Of Dr Caligari" which features a Floydianhypnotic bass groove accompanied by fiery Eloy inspired keyboard attacks. The addition of the fluteoffers some nice touches while the bass thumps and the guitar initiates its trickery and likewise"The Light Of Metropolis" offers more of the same albeit with an entirely different melodicunderpinning. However the track lacks the sense of dread that the film conveyed so well. "Workers"is perhaps the closest thing a true dark sounding track with nice fuzzy bass tones but even thisfalls short of what the album cover art portends. "Frankenstein" offers some nice jaw harp andkeyboard wizardry but once again what should be more in the Goblin playbook given the theme comesoff as a rather breezy symphonic walk in the park but does pick up tempo and offers some of the morerockin' moments.The album slightly tapers off in quality towards the end. Overall this was one that made a nicefirst impression but like Morte Macabre and similarly minded acts fails to sustain my interest asthis type of thing has been done so well by Goblin and other horror prog acts. In the end it's apleasure to listen to a couple times but not quite up to par with many of the true darker progclassics whether they be from early Univers Zero or the plethora of darkened zeuhl and avant-progthat kept the 80s underground humming along. Nice keyboard workouts and instrumental workouts and ifyou prefer a much lighter sound for this kind of music then you might be more invigorated by it thani am. Still though, a nice semi-unique offering by a rather unknown band from Russia.
items._genre: symphonic prog / crossover prog / space rock / instrumental
items._cn_summary: ENINE 来自俄罗斯弗拉基米尔，是一支以吉他为主导的器乐前卫摇滚乐队。这张专辑以1910至1920年代默片时代的恐怖与科幻电影为主题，灵感涵盖《卡里加里博士》《诺斯费拉图》《大都会》《弗兰肯斯坦》等经典。音乐融合了70年代Eloy的交响摇滚气质、Pink Floyd的迷幻律动与Camel、Genesis式的键盘铺陈，同时加入长笛、口琴等元素增添层次。整体风格偏向交响化的空间摇滚即兴，但并未真正营造出默片恐怖片所应有的阴暗氛围，听感更像是轻盈的漫步而非压迫感。专辑前半部分质量最佳，开篇几首曲目在键盘攻击性与贝斯律动之间取得平衡，末尾部分略显疲软。乐评指出作品缺乏Goblin等恐怖前卫乐队那种持续的张力，整体印象尚可但难以多次聆听。

items.body: Review by Stefano61 — There is a particular stretch of English coast, in Yorkshire, where the North Sea arrives already telling stories before it reaches the shore. In 1890 a Dublin theatre manager on holiday there climbed the long run of steps up to the abbey ruins above the harbour, heard the local tale of a storm driven ship that ran aground with its entire crew already dead, and went home to write the most famous shipwreck in English fiction. Bram Stoker never lived in Whitby. He only visited, and the town gave him nightmares he carried for the rest of his career.A century later it gave something gentler, though no less powerful, to a boy who did live there, listening from his bedroom to the same water arriving against the same cliffs in winter. Steve Rothery grew up in Whitby. Decades later, looking for somewhere to begin a record with an old friend, he did not reach for a studio concept. He walked Steve Hackett along that same coast and showed him where it had all started.Between them the two guitarists carry over half a century of British progressive music. Hackett spent the first half of the nineteen seventies inside Genesis, shaping some of that band's most enduring guitar writing before a long, prolific solo career that in 2018 finally let him revisit that early material live, with a full band and orchestra behind him. Rothery has been the sound of Marillion's guitar since the band's earliest days, a voice built less on speed than on sustain, on knowing exactly how long to hold a note before letting it go. The two men had circled each other's orbit for decades without ever actually making a record together, until this one.The Roaring Waves took the better part of a decade to arrive, worked on intermittently between tours and other commitments, in sessions at Rothery's own studio in Buckinghamshire and in both men's homes. Hackett has described the approach as deliberately old fashioned, closer to friends gathering in a garage than to any formal writing session, built from jams and shared ideas rather than material arriving pre written. Rothery, used to working this way from Marillion's own methods, found the looseness familiar. Hackett, whose long collaboration with the Hungarian band Djabe had already taught him something about improvising inside someone else's musical language, took a little longer to settle into it. What both men insisted on, repeatedly, was that neither should try to outplay the other. The record was to paint with sound rather than race across it.They are joined by the Italian musician Riccardo Romano, who plays keyboards and bass, produced and mixed the record, and co wrote three of its seven pieces, alongside drummers Daniele Pomo, across the first five tracks, and Leon Parr, who takes over for the last two. Romano and Pomo already knew Rothery's music from the inside, having played for years in his own solo band, and it shows in how naturally they hold the ground beneath two guitarists who could easily have crowded each other out.Seven instrumental pieces, nothing sung, everything said through guitar, and one subject holding the whole record together: the sea, and everything memory and imagination have ever hung on it. The record does not stay in Yorkshire. It begins there, at the harbour Rothery grew up beside, then drifts outward toward waters that have nothing to do with his childhood at all, a vanished Cold War submarine, a contested inland sea, an American highway running the length of an entirely different ocean, as though one coastline, looked at closely enough, always leads a person back out to every other.- The Storm: the album's overture and its most turbulent piece, opening on Riccardo Romano's simulated strings before Hackett enters with dramatic, almost marching guitar lines, power chords, and Daniele Pomo's drums arriving as though in procession behind him. The two guitarists trade call and response phrases across a vamp stretched taut but never quite breaking, the closest the record comes to outright aggression before the sea, as it always eventually does, calms.- Sandsend: named for the small village just along the coast from Whitby, and the record's first real exhale, its main melody so vocal in shape it could almost be sung. Where The Storm gave the coastline its ferocity, Sandsend gives it wonder, a gentle rise and fall of guitar over patient drumming and understated bass, evoking a childhood spent walking that particular stretch of sand rather than fearing it. Rothery has spoken of the place as somewhere genuinely touched by magic, and the piece carries that without ever needing to say so directly.- Red Dragon: named after a seventeenth century East India Company ship, and the record's most overtly adventurous piece, opening on the drone of a hurdy gurdy, an instrument that reaches back to medieval Europe, before Rothery's riff turns heavy and Hackett answers with sitar guitar and melodic lines chasing an unmistakably Eastern flavour. A d�tour east, briefly, before the record returns to its own coastline.- The Roaring Waves: the title piece, and the record's centre of gravity, opening on Hackett's fingerpicked nylon string guitar before orchestral strings rise beneath a single soaring melody that eventually erupts into a full blooded solo. The two guitarists close it out in genuine duet, before the whole thing settles into an acoustic coda carried by piano, tension gathered and then, finally, allowed to rest.- K-129: named for a Soviet submarine lost in the Pacific in 1968 with its entire crew, its true fate still disputed decades later. The piece opens on a looping, mechanical pulse standing in for the vessel's own repeated motion through the water, ghostly sonar pings drifting through the mix, Rothery's playing staying melodic even as Hackett pushes toward distortion and noise. It is the moment on the record that leans furthest from guitar rock and closest to Rothery's own recent electronic collaborations, nearer Tangerine Dream than Marillion, before the two guitars eventually surface again together.- The Black Sea: the record's slowest, most reflective piece, built on restraint rather than notes played fast, and all the more affecting for it. Depth, isolation, pressure, everything the title promises, delivered through melody rather than volume.- Pacific Coast Highway: the closing piece, and a genuine change of climate, harmonica and quick, bright riffs pulling the record decisively out of its own melancholy and toward something closer to blues rock, fast and warm and, after six pieces built largely on weather and depth, almost startlingly sunlit. An unexpected way to end a record about the sea, and exactly right for it.What makes The Roaring Waves work is not really its instrumental fireworks, though there is no shortage of those, but its refusal to stay in one place. It begins as a very personal record, one man's coastline handed to an old friend as a way of explaining himself, and ends up as something closer to a history of the sea itself, its wrecks, its wars, its holiday postcards.Two guitarists who could easily have spent seven tracks proving who was faster instead spent them listening to each other, and the record is better for the restraint. If it has a fault, it is one earned honestly: built largely from jams rather than pre written songs, the middle stretch occasionally lets atmosphere do work a sharper melodic idea might have done better, and this is a record that rewards patient, attentive listening rather than a single pass in the car.Coming from two men in their sixties and seventies who had never previously made a record together, that patience feels less like a flaw than like the whole point. Whitby gave Bram Stoker a nightmare that outlived him by more than a century. It has now given Steve Hackett and Steve Rothery something gentler and, in its own way, just as lasting. My rating: 4/5.(Bassano del Grappa, September 2026)
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑是两位英国前卫摇滚吉他老将的首次正式合作：Genesis前成员Steve Hackett与Marillion主音吉他手Steve Rothery。制作历时近十年，采取极为松散的方式——在录音室即兴碰撞、共同积累素材，而非预先写好曲式。键盘手兼贝斯手Riccardo Romano参与共同创作并担任制作人，鼓手Daniele Pomo与Leon Parr分别负责前后半段的节奏铺垫。两人刻意避免炫技式竞速，转而以音色与延音营造空间感。整张唱片扎根于英格兰约克郡海岸的自然与人文背景，从Whitby小镇的海风与悬崖中获得灵感。录音地点包括Rothery位于白金汉郡的个人工作室及两人各自的住所，呈现出一对老友在车库里合奏般的私密氛围，而非概念化的工作室产物。

items.body: Review by SeeHatfield — I know next to nothing about the history of PFM (apart from what I've read here on Prog Archives and on Wikipedia), and I couldn't name the band's members without referencing a cheat sheet. I usually don't have any idea of what they're singing about, either. But I've been listening to them on and off for the better part of forty years, and I know their first five studio albums (plus the English-language adaptations of two of them). I thank a prog-loving friend for making me a tape of Storia Di Un Minuto and its follow-up, Per Un Amico, back in my undergrad days; those two albums in particular cast a spell on me.Without ever researching the lyrics or the band, I came to love those two records (even as I somehow lost or ditched my copy of the English-language Photos of Ghosts along the way). I've come to realize that I greatly prefer the very early PFM, when it included flautist and violinist Mauro Pagani and did not yet include vocalist Bernardo Lanzetti. I think those were the prime years.Storia Di Un Minuto must surely count as one of the great debuts in progressive rock. It's tuneful, inventive, dynamic, and fun, channeling obvious Crimso and Tull influences in the direction of richly melodic, romantic Italianicity. It's eminently hummable, an album of great themes and fragments, with so many moments that stick in my mind. I won't go into detail, but must note that this is exactly what I like about vintage prog: the feeling of several musicians putting their heads and hands together and treating the studio like a laboratory. There's a lot of skill in these five players, but more important than their chops is their enthusiasm for raiding the rag basket, stitching together so many disparate elements, and pushing themselves past their limits. There's a shamelessness about this kind of music, and a sheer love of discovery. Storia Di Un Minuto, at just under 35 minutes, is so full of good stuff that it's a bit of a miracle."Impressioni di Settembre," with its upward-straining melodic hook at the end of each verse (that lovely upsurge of mellotron and Moog), is PFM's "Crimson King," while "La Carrozza di Hans" weds Tullish flute to a frantic, "Schizoid Man"-style 6/8 section and, "Aqualung"-style, jams together different bits into a frantic musical puzzle. These moves are familiar, but with PFM the delight is the distinctiveness of their own melodies. Also, the singing, though divvied up among several members, is good throughout (I've never thought of Lanzetti as an improvement). In a few years, PFM would crank up the heavy rock, bank on their skill, and lose some of their early delicacy (listen to the virtuosic hammering of Chocolate Kings to know what I mean). I think that's too bad. The good stuff was the exploratory early stuff, which happened to birth some excellent songs and lovely scraps. Maybe I should figure out the lyrics now?

items._cn_summary: 1972年意大利前卫摇滚乐队PFM的处女作，以丰富的旋律性、动态编排和实验精神著称。专辑时长不到35分钟，却融合了King Crimson式的力量和Jethro Tull式的长笛元素，形成独特的意大利抒情风格。评论者特别强调早期PFM的精致与探索性，认为乐队在后续作品中转向更重的摇滚路线后失去了这些特质。音乐呈现多位乐手在录音室中即兴实验的状态，技术精湛但更重要的是将各种不同元素拼贴融合的热情。歌曲如'Impressioni di Settembre'以mellotron和Moog的上升旋律令人难忘，'La Carrozza di Hans'则将长笛与复杂的6/8拍节奏结合。整体展现出七十年代初意大利前卫摇滚特有的浪漫气质与冒险精神，是该领域的经典开篇之作。

items.body: Liars will release their new album A Ban On Plastic Bag Bans through Mute Records on 5 March 2027. The band, now the solo recording vehicle of Angus Andrew, has shared the first single, “Ice Pick, Kalamazoo,” alongside UK and European tour dates in October. “Ice Pick, Kalamazoo” takes its title from the city in Michigan where Andrew relocated with his wife and daughter. Soon after moving, he noticed a persistent smell around the family home and his daughter’s school, traced to hydrogen sulphide and other pollutants released by a local packaging factory at levels the state health department flagged as dangerous enough to advise residents to stay indoors. Andrew got involved in a campaign to hold the factory accountable, and the experience, and its tangle of environmental damage, corporate responsibility and bureaucratic inertia, became the starting point for the new album. “A Ban On Plastic Bag Bans” takes its title from an actual Michigan statute that bars local governments from banning single-use plastic bags, a piece of legislation Andrew found emblematic of how attempts to reduce environmental harm can themselves become targets for prohibition. “You become so used to something, you lose your sense of it,” Andrew said of the theme running through the record: how injustice settles into the background of daily life, and how draining it becomes to keep pushing against institutions built to outlast that resistance. The album was written and recorded across the United States and Australia, where Andrew now lives, in collaboration with drummer Laurence Pike and multi-instrumentalist Cameron Deyell, both of whom worked on 2021’s “The Apple Drop” and have toured with Liars since 2017’s “TFCF”. Rather than building the songs from finished demos, the three musicians worked through improvisation, developing material across continents by ear rather than by score. Andrew describes the result as a different kind of political record, one concerned less with protest itself than with the toll of sustaining it. “It wasn’t just the environment that was polluted,” he said. “It was also my mind.” “A Ban On Plastic Bag Bans” will be released on white recycled and recyclable PET vinyl, CD and digital formats. The tracklist runs: “Happy Or Not,” “Ice Pick, Kalamazoo,” “Laced Plume,” “Urgent As Always,” “Deep Deeper,” “Disaster Tropes,” “Beat Creep Some Eyes,” “Real Time Trespasser,” “SHAME!,” “Retention Arc” and “Out Of Order.” The period leading up to the album followed the disruption of the pandemic, when touring plans for “The Apple Drop” fell through and Andrew stepped back from making new Liars music for the first time since his teens. He spent the time on other projects instead, founding the record label No Gold and the experimental platform Essential Tremors. “Both of those things were really about listening,” he said, describing the shift away from being “a full-time creator” toward closer engagement with other artists and with his adopted surroundings in Kalamazoo. Liars tour dates for ‘A Ban On Plastic Bag Bans’ The album announcement comes with UK and European tour dates, giving audiences a rare chance to see the band’s live show in intimate rooms, plus a one-off 20th-anniversary performance of “Drums Not Dead” with two Polish percussionists, including Macio Moretti, at Unsound Festival. Tickets go on sale from 10am local time on 11 September via the band’s official site. 2 October – Bucharest, Romania – Control Club (Opening Party) 3 October – Nantes, France – Le Lieu Unique 5 October – Milan, Italy – Arci Bellezza 9 October – Krakow, Poland – Unsound Festival (“Drums Not Dead” 20th-anniversary performance) 10 October – Belgrade, Serbia – Changeover Festival 12 October – Prague, Czech Republic – Punctum 13 October – Berlin, Germany – Neue Zukunft 15 October – Amsterdam, Netherlands – Paradiso 17 October – Kortrijk, Belgium – Atelier Nooitgedacht 18 October – Liege, Belgium – Kultura 20 October – London, UK – Moth Club 22 October – Paris, France – Boule Noire 24 October – Copenhagen, Denmark – Ideal Bar About Liars Angus Andrew and Aaron Hemphill met in the late 1990s in Los Angeles, where Andrew was studying photography at CalArts and Hemphill worked at a local record store. The two began recording together before relocating to New York, where they answered a musicians’ wanted ad from bassist Pat Noecker and drummer Ron Albertson. The four-piece was formally christened Liars in New York in November 2000. Working with producer Steve Revitte, the band recorded its debut album, “They Threw Us All in a Trench and Stuck a Monument on Top,” in two days; it was released in October 2001 on Gern Blandsten Records, with Blast First and later Mute Records handling subsequent reissues. Albertson left the band in 2000 before the debut’s release, and Noecker departed in 2002; multi-instrumentalist Julian Gross joined in 2003. Liars moved to Mute Records for 2004’s “They Were Wrong, So We Drowned” and continued releasing albums on the label through 2006’s “Drums Not Dead,” their self-titled 2007 album, 2010’s “Sisterworld,” 2012’s “WIXIW,” 2014’s “Mess,” 2017’s “TFCF” and 2021’s “The Apple Drop.” Hemphill left the band amicably around the release of “TFCF,” after which Andrew continued Liars as a solo recording project, working with a rotating cast of collaborators including Laurence Pike and Cameron Deyell. Since “The Apple Drop,” Andrew has also run the label No Gold and the experimental platform Essential Tremors from Australia, where he now lives. “A Ban On Plastic Bag Bans,” due 5 March 2027 on Mute, is Liars’ tenth studio album and their first release since “The Apple Drop,” accompanied by their first UK and European live dates in years.
items._cn_summary: Liars新专辑由Angus Andrew作为唯一核心成员，联合鼓手Laurence Pike与多乐器演奏者Cameron Deyell，以跨大洲远程即兴方式创作完成，摒弃成品小样，依赖听觉协作发展素材。主题源于Andrew迁居密歇根Kalamazoo后的亲身经历：当地包装工厂释放硫化氢等污染物，州卫生部门建议居民留在室内；他参与问责运动，由此延伸至环境损害、企业责任与制度惰性的交织。专辑标题取自一项禁止地方政府限制一次性塑料袋的密歇根州法令，Andrew以此隐喻环保努力本身如何被反向压制。Andrew形容这是一张关于持续抗争之消耗、而非抗议本身的政治唱片。唱片将以白色再生PET黑胶、CD及数字格式发行。整体内容偏新闻稿性质，缺乏对实际音乐声响与创新的具体描述。

items.body: Review by Fercandio46 — Much has been written about this album, and much more will be, since ultimately, it is up to each listener to decide which era they enjoy most; that is precisely what makes it valuable. However, if we are to exchange impressions, I must say that as a lifelong Jethro Tull fan, I really liked Too Old to Rock 'n' Roll: Too Young to Die! just as it is. Simpler in structure and composition than its predecessors, it completes an arc spanning the entire decade of the 70s, moving from raw blues and jazz to elaborate progressive rock, and then (following Minstrel in the Gallery as the swan song of their grand epics) continuing with a run of solid albums featuring acoustic folk-rock and flute-driven rock, leading up to Stormwatch in 1979.The recording style itself featured a distinct, more modern vocal echo; the string arrangements on "Quizz Kid" were just as classic as those they had used previously, and Ian Anderson's voice remained in perfect form'though now serving songs of a simpler construction that drew partly from 50s rock while also incorporating classical influences. The brass section added a fresh tone, and whenever a song shifted to a slower section, the arrangements remained delicate and intricate, evoking old waltzes that coexisted with a modern sound hovering somewhere between glam and new wave. Yet, somehow, they made it all work for me, Martin Barre's guitar, Ian's flute, and a band sounding incredibly tight.I have a real soft spot for "Crazed Institution," and I always loved how they blended the bass and acoustic guitar. They were really playing around with the arrangement, electric guitar appearing and fading out, piano coming in and dropping away. "Salamander" captures the full power of Barre's guitar, a perfect counterpart to Ian's vocals, and traverses so many musical landscapes and tonal colors before the singing even begins; it is a marvel to listen to. How, then, can anyone say the album doesn't measure up? When they started out, they dressed like rag-and-bone men, wandering alleys with dogs, wearing little more than an old overcoat or a bowler hat; later came the capes and tights, so why couldn't they change again? To me, it was a very dignified shift where the quality of the music remained intact; it was their signature style, without ever betraying who they were."Taxi Grab" has a vibe that sits somewhere between Western and glam; it sounds like classic Tull, bluesy, yet also modern and cool. Not to mention the variety of styles Barre executes, along with the subtle variations where they played with and subverted the genres they were channeling. These moments are scattered throughout, waiting to be discovered by anyone willing to look for them."From A Dead Beat To An Old Greaser" has the same ingredients as songs from the past but is modernized with a Rhodes keyboard and a saxophone that comes in later; there's a touch of country-western, too, yet it ends up sounding jazzy, almost like cabaret music. To me, they pull it off very naturally, partly because of the strings, which pair perfectly with Ian's vocals. John Glascock's bass playing proves fundamental to the album's sound."Bad-Eyed and Loveless" has a flamenco touch; Barre's acoustic guitar and Anderson's vocals shine, enhanced by that echo effect that suited them so well, creating space through silence in introductions that could stretch on indefinitely, as they never repeated in the same way throughout the song. Beyond technical quality, they held something else for me: genuine feeling, the other essential ingredient of music. "Big Dipper" featured subtle details tucked into the chorus alongside John Evan's piano, paving the way for "Too Old to Rock 'n' Roll: Too Young to Die", the album's title track, a signature song, and a virtual statement of principles that instantly became a new classic for the band. I remember the Tampa, Florida show, not because I was there (I was just being born around that time!), but because I've seen the footage and witnessed the deep emotion with which these songs were performed. Like the tracks on the albums that followed, they resonated powerfully with me, marking a distinct, intense phase in the band's evolution. The 50s rock 'n' roll format intersects with classical elements, where wind instruments and guitar engage in Bach-like counterpoint, and strings come together to create an unforgettable song that is 100% Tull."Pied Piper" is another great acoustic gem, overflowing with ideas and subtle melodies from a flautist who keeps one foot in the forest and the other on the city pavement. A classic chorus would emerge out of nowhere, with his magnificent voice gracing every song; at times his singing would quicken, making it a delight to hear alongside the pizzicato violins.Perhaps "The Chequered Flag (Dead or Alive)" could be considered a concession to a more commercial sound... yet it also features classical echoes and a magnificently integrated string section, all full of emotion. So, for me, Too Old To Rock 'n' Roll: Too Young To Die! will always be an album that warms the heart, in a different way from its predecessors, certainly, but also marking the start of a new and equally great era of albums that would last until the end of the decade.
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑是Jethro Tull在七十年代转型期的作品，从早期蓝调爵士与繁复前卫摇滚逐渐转向以民谣摇滚和长笛驱动的结构化歌曲。评论者认为专辑虽比前作简约，却保留了乐队标志性的编制风格——Martin Barre的吉他、Ian Anderson的嗓音与长笛，以及弦乐与铜管的编配。歌曲构建巧妙，如《Crazed Institution》中贝斯与木吉他的交织、《Salamander》中吉他音色的多变、《Taxi Grab》西部与华丽摇滚的杂糅，以及《From A Dead Beat To An Old Greaser》中爵士与卡巴莱气质的融合，都体现了乐队在类型间的游走能力。整体而言，这是一张编排精致、气质内敛的前卫民谣摇滚专辑，融合了古典、华丽摇滚与五十年代摇滚元素。

items.body: Review by ianjferris@gmail.com — Last week, at a small record & cd fair in a little community based local hall in County Wicklow, I flicked through a sale bin of old records. Three albums therein caught my attention - Olias Of Sunhillow by Jon Anderson, Hergest Ridge by Mike Oldfield and Five Bridges by The Nice (the subject of this review). All were in excellent condition and I secured the three for ?20. Olias of Sunhillow (particularly) and Hergest Ridge were excellent purchases. Five Bridges however, is just not my cup of tea. I completely understand Keith Emerson's talented approach to this album but really, it's contents are just overbloated self indulgent piffle, much in the same vein as the later Pictures at an Exhibition, which was also helmed by Emerson In Chief. While Five Bridges isn't without a few brief nice moments (pun completely intended), the fact is they are just that, a few brief moments. So it's not for me. Sorry to all you Nice fans out there but it's just 2 stars (it would have been one star except for the fact that when I awarded only one star to Pictures At An Exhibition, Progarchives wouldn't publish my review 😊 - probably right too because it was a bit scathing). Collectors, dedicated fans and completionists only. I hope to offload the album soon, to a shop in Dublin which deals secondhand records.
items._cn_summary: 评论者认为，这张专辑试图把摇滚乐队与交响编制结合，并突出键盘手基思·埃默森的炫技与主导地位。其音乐虽具备一定技术含量，也能产生若干短促而鲜明的段落，但整体被批评为篇幅臃肿、过度自我展示，结构与持续吸引力不足。评论尤其将其与埃默森后来参与制作的《展览会之画》相比较，认为两者存在相似的缺点，因此更适合执着于该乐队或希望补全收藏的听众，而非偏爱实验、爵士或跨领域融合的听者。

items.body: Clan of Xymox released “Farewell” on 8 September 2003 through Metropolis Records in the US. The album turns 23 this year. A Discogs listing for the same US CD pressing shows a street date of 25 August 2003; Metropolis’s own catalogue and MusicBrainz both confirm 8 September as the release date. Ronny Moorings wrote, recorded and mixed the album, co-producing it with Mojca at The Torture Chamber in Amsterdam. Dierk Budde mastered it at Voodoogarden Studio. What is on Clan of Xymox’s ‘Farewell’ The album runs 10 tracks: “Farewell”, “Cold Damp Day”, “There’s No Tomorrow”, “Dark Mood”, “One More Time”, “Into Extremes”, “It’s Not Enough”, “Courageous”, “Losing My Head” and “Skindeep”, with a total running time of just over 59 minutes. Mojca designed the sleeve. The title track received an official video. About Clan of Xymox Clan of Xymox formed in Nijmegen, the Netherlands, in 1981 under the name Xymox, led by Ronny Moorings. The band signed to 4AD and released its debut album, “Clan of Xymox”, in 1985, followed by “Medusa” in 1986, both defining releases in the darkwave and goth rock scene of the period. A move to Polydor and a shortened band name, Xymox, produced “Twist of Shadows” (1989) and “Phoenix” (1991), after which the band’s major-label run ended. Moorings revived the project as Clan of Xymox in 1997, beginning a run of studio albums on Metropolis Records that included “Hidden Faces” (1997), “Notes From The Underground” (2001), “Farewell” (2003) and later albums through the 2000s and 2010s. Side-Line has tracked the band’s catalogue over the years, including Clan of Xymox’s ‘In Love We Trust’ turns 17 on 18 August. Moorings has kept the band active on tour and in the studio into the 2020s, continuing a discography that now spans more than four decades.
items._cn_summary: 这篇文章并非真正的乐评，而是Side-Line杂志发布的纪念性新闻稿，纪念Clan of Xymox 2003年专辑《Farewell》发行23周年。文章主要罗列了专辑的基本信息：发行日期、厂牌、制作人员、曲目列表，以及乐队从1981年成立至今的简要历史回顾。专辑由Ronny Moorings独自在阿姆斯特丹The Torture Chamber工作室创作、录制并混音，Dierk Budde负责母带处理，共收录10首曲目，时长约59分钟。内容缺少对音乐本身的分析、评论或评价，仅作为档案性信息整理发布。Clan of Xymox是荷兰暗潮/哥特摇滚领域的标志性乐队，4AD厂牌时期的作品对后世影响深远，《Farewell》延续了其电子化暗潮风格，但文章未能深入探讨其音乐特色。

items.body: Purple Trash release their new album “Velvet Nightmares and Cold Sleep” on Swiss Dark Nights. The twelve-track record is out now on digiCD, moving between darkwave, gothic rock, post-punk and electronica. Purple Trash is the solo project of Sergio Da Silva, also known as Bornyhake, a Swiss multi-instrumentalist and composer who has been active on the Swiss underground scene for over twenty-five years and who founded the band Borgne in the 1990s. Da Silva launched Purple Trash in 2020, and “Velvet Nightmares and Cold Sleep” pushes the project deeper into a claustrophobic, self-contained sound, moving between slower, melancholic passages and more electronic, rhythmic territory. Opener “The Echoes of a Sleeping Mind” sets a melancholic tone built around guitar and vocals within its first two minutes, while “Scatterbrain Cathedral” follows with electric guitar and a heavier electronic arrangement. The album’s rhythm section pushes hardest on “It’s a Funeral Pyre”, before “I Tried to Sniff Coffee” returns to a bleaker, more introspective register that runs through the rest of the record. The full tracklist reads “The Echoes of a Sleeping Mind”, “Scatterbrain Cathedral”, “Ashes of Desire”, “I’m Hacking Like a Broke-Down Car”, “Walls Without Names”, “It’s a Funeral Pyre”, “I Tried to Sniff Coffee”, “Chains Made of Gold”, “Through a Forest of Tobacco Trees”, “I Was a Trash Can”, “Feathers in the Shadows” and “A Morning Beyond All Worry”. Velvet Nightmares and Cold Sleep by Purple Trash About Purple Trash Purple Trash is the solo project of Swiss musician Sergio Da Silva, known under the alias Bornyhake, who has been active on the Swiss underground scene for more than twenty-five years. Da Silva founded the band Borgne in the 1990s, entwining ethereal melodies with drum machines. He launched Purple Trash as a solo outlet in 2020, moving between darkwave, gothic rock, post-punk and electronica while keeping the dark, unsettling atmospheres that run through his other work. “Velvet Nightmares and Cold Sleep”, released through Swiss Dark Nights, is his latest album under the Purple Trash name.
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑是瑞士地下音乐人Sergio Da Silva以Purple Trash之名发布的十二首作品，跨越暗潮、哥特摇滚、后朋克与电子乐之间。开篇曲目以吉他与人声奠定忧郁基调，随后转向更厚重的电子编曲，节奏段落在特定曲目中推向最强力度，后续则回归内省阴郁的氛围。整体声响呈现出幽闭、自我封闭的气质，在慢速忧郁段落与电子律动之间反复切换。Da Silva自九十年代起活跃于瑞士地下场景，此前创建了将空灵旋律与鼓机结合的乐队Borgne，Purple Trash延续了这一脉络，专辑由瑞士独立厂牌Swiss Dark Nights以数字CD形式发行。文章本身更接近新闻稿性质，缺乏深度评论与个性化视角，对声音设计与艺术意图的阐述较为有限。

items.body:
Hopeful Melodies Pair With Grief & Anxiety-Inspired Lyrics On Lotus Flower's 'A Night of the Jumps'

8 September 2026

When he chose the moniker 'Lotus Flower' for himself, it was clear Shriraj Sagara wasn't trying to hide that he is influenced by Radiohead, his voice often choosing the relaxed, high-pitched falsetto singing that has defined frontman Thom Yorke's work. The Ahmedabad-rooted, Berlin-based musician continues to gradually build upon that influence in his latest EP 'A Night of the Jumps'.

The melodies of the falsetto singing lend more to the atmosphere of synth arpeggios, horn lines and steady percussion rather than inviting the limelight. Meanwhile, Shriraj's compositions carry a more uplifting quality even as they deal with an unsettled mixture of anxiety, grief and vulnerability. Notably, the pounding rhythm section of opener 'Ceremony', unlike the formerly mentioned namesake influence, keeps things more communal and inviting than introspective, even as the song attempts to capture the coldness and disorientation of a difficult winter.

The subtly gritty and detuned synth foundations of 'A Small Town Cries' harken more to the nostalgia found in works by acts like Boards of Canada, though the lyrics draw from fragments of news from Israel's war on Gaza. The track Shriraj join hands again with his brother Shantanu Sagara for another DIY music video, though with less production value than their previous stellar work 'Wilting'.

Check out 'A Night of the Jumps' below and follow Shriraj Sagara on Instagram for more information.

items._cn_summary: 这张EP围绕焦虑、悲伤与脆弱展开，却用上扬的旋律线条和合成器琶音构建出明亮氛围，形成情绪上的反差。假声演唱融入合成器层次与铜管旋律，编曲以氛围铺陈为主而非突出人声。开篇曲的鼓击节奏营造出社区感的律动，与New Order同名曲的冷峻内省形成对比。第二首则使用略带粗糙和失谐的合成器质感，唤起Boards of Canada式的怀旧情绪，歌词取材自加沙战争相关的新闻碎片。整体制作倾向于DIY路线，音乐录影带由艺术家与其兄弟合作完成。旋律与歌词之间形成一种错位：表面温暖，内核沉重，适合关注当代独立电子与情感叙事的听众。
